Use generous breathing room, cream parchment and midnight navy framing, fine muted gold rules, readable typography. Boss remains imposing. Culture and cast: warm human faces; compact blue-cloaked adventurer, broad adult plated guard, apron weaponsmith Brann, armored Tessa, elder staff merchant Orin. Environment, colors, materials: royal blue, ivory, field green, muted gold; oak, steel, linen; rolling fields, stone arches, timber market, distant King's Keep. Boss: enchanted empty royal armor, crowned helm, huge sword and shield, burgundy cape in a ruined throne hall. Show shared equipable weapons, shield, staff and practical cultural objects as separate studies; do not suggest lineage-exclusive classes. Reference image 1 supplies only the relevant lineage silhouette from the eight-character showcase; reference image 2 supplies only this boss design, never its HUD or other bosses. Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: landscape world-region moodboard, matching the existing fantasy RPG art-direction atlas.
Create ONE beautiful, detailed, legible moodboard titled exactly "THE ABANDONED CITY OF BABYLON", subtitle "Ruins • Tower • Depths". This is an original fantasy-game location, not a historical reconstruction.
Reference image 1 is the approved Nimrod boss and Babylonian tower visual reference: retain his dark beard, tall blue/gold crown, blue scale armor, burgundy cape, lion-headed mace and floating royal decree tablets. Do not copy gameplay HUD.
Reference image 2 supplies the moodboard layout, parchment, navy/gold framing and painted game-art style only; do NOT copy goblin architecture or its rat boss.
Make the environment dominate, with clearly distinct panels and short exact labels:
1) Large upper-left panoramic "Abandoned City": sun-bleached collapsed ziggurat terraces, monumental broken blue-glazed brick gates with weathered lion reliefs, dry canals, hanging bazaar ruins, windblown sand and sparse overgrowth. The Broken Concourse holds only a tiny exchange broker and a few cross-lineage wanderers, not a thriving city.
2) Large upper-center vertical landmark "Tower of Babylon": colossal leaning stepped spiral tower of ancient brick, lapis-blue tile and tarnished gold rising above the ruined city, broken terraces, a shattered astronomical observatory at its summit, tiny side-scrolling ledges and an ominous entrance into the buried foundations. Show whole recognizable tower silhouette.
3) Upper-right smaller boss concept "Nimrod": full-body powerful king matching reference, on a ruined tower terrace, no UI.
4) Three equally prominent lower environment vignettes: "Dungeon • Flooded Vaults" (submerged masonry, broken stairs, inscription tablets, sunken library shelves, ruined orrery and blue torchlight); "Swamp • Drowned Canals" (misty reeds, twisted roots, algae-green canals overtaking the distant city margins, half-sunken reliefs, rotten plank platforms and faint bioluminescence); "Caves • Buried Foundations" (natural dark limestone caverns meeting buried ancient brick, stalactites, crystal glints, underground river and broken stone bridges). Swamp and caves are distinct exploratory subarea concepts; do not replace the dry surface city with a swamp.
Bottom narrow strip: small proposed Exchange Broker, Lorekeeper and Relic Explorer concepts, a clay tablet, blue-glazed brick, bronze astrolabe, ruined lion carving, five material/color swatches. Short labels only.
Mood: abandoned grandeur, quiet mystery, ancient astronomical magic, inviting exploration. Child-friendly cinematic storybook fantasy, lush painterly environment layers and crisp small 3.5–4-head-tall characters; original ornamental language. Palette: weathered sandstone, lapis blue, tarnished gold, marsh green, cavern teal, warm torch amber. Clear readable typography, art-book composition, navy borders and warm parchment gutters. No health bars, no game buttons, no gore, no giant blocks of prose, no modern city, no photorealism, no watermark. Render at a large landscape aspect ratio with enough space to inspect all five environments separately.

Use case: style-transfer.
Edit reference image 1, the Babylon moodboard, into a clearly SIMPLER STORYBOOK GAME-ART version. Keep its entire panel layout, all exact titles and labels, all five environments, three NPC roles, cultural objects, palette, and abandoned Babylon identity. Reference image 2 is the STRICT desired rendering language and Nimrod design. This is a substantial style transformation of ALL ENVIRONMENTS, not merely inserting a cartoon boss into unchanged realistic scenery.

Replace Nimrod in the top-right panel with the compact, outlined blue/gold/burgundy king from reference 2: large head, short legs, broad body, simple beard, lion mace, three decree tablets.
Apply that same graphic language to every map panel:
- Large readable simplified architectural shapes, thick pillars, chunky oversized sandstone blocks, broad arches, big blue glazed tiles with single simple lion motifs. Draw only a few block seams rather than every brick.
- Tower of Babylon: an iconic stepped, slightly leaning tower with 5–7 major tiers, broad terraces and simplified broken orrery rings at the summit; clearly legible silhouette, no forest of tiny arches and spires. Remain monumental and abandoned.
- Abandoned City: broken oversized gate, a clear continuous side-scrolling road in the foreground, sparse chunky ruined buildings, a few compact wandering NPCs and one broker stall; dry canals and windblown sand. Do not make it a thriving city.
- Dungeon / Flooded Vaults: clear broad ledges and stairs above simple blue water shapes, a few thick pillars, one large broken astronomical mechanism. Distinguish walkable surfaces from background.
- Swamp / Drowned Canals: rounded reed clusters, broad twisted roots, simple moss masses, clear plank walkway across muted green water; distant ruins rendered softly.
- Caves / Buried Foundations: broad rock planes, 4–6 chunky stalactites, grouped crystal shapes, a clear bridge/platform route over a simple underground stream, embedded blue-brick ruins.
All scenery should have clean dark contours on foreground shapes, broad local colors, two or three soft cel-shaded values, smooth painted surfaces, gentle atmospheric depth and restrained highlights. Backgrounds softer and lower contrast, walkable plane crisp. No photorealistic textures, tiny scratches, dense brick patterns, glittering reflections, harsh cinematic spotlights or high-frequency rubble. More visual breathing room between objects. Rich color and mystery without detail noise. Match the stylized character in reference 2, not realistic matte painting.
NPCs and objects along the bottom also get compact proportions, simple readable silhouettes, big hands, rounded forms, bold outlines and limited shading. Preserve all exact text, including "THE ABANDONED CITY OF BABYLON", "Tower of Babylon", "Nimrod", and the dungeon/swamp/caves labels. Preserve navy/parchment framing, simplify incidental border texture. No added panels, UI, or explanatory paragraphs. Large landscape image, polished coherent art-direction board.
